newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HUNGRY FEYENOORD WAIT FOR DEPLETED AJAX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HUNGRY FEYENOORD WAIT FOR DEPLETED AJAX.

text.p: Ajax Amsterdam, struggling to keep in touch with the Dutch first division pacemakers, go into Sunday's clash with Feyenoord with over half the first-team missing and morale ebbing away.
Coach Louis van Gaal will be without the bedrock of his defence, with skipper Danny Blind recovering from a groin operation and Frank de Boer nursing a damaged left ankle.
Brazilian World Cup-winning defender Santos is out of favour but may be drafted back into the side after being suspended for Wednesday's 2-1 home defeat by Auxerre in the Champions' league.

Right-back John Veldman will struggle to find a place. He was at fault for one of NAC's goals in a 2-0 league defeat last weekend and was substituted after just 23 minutes against Auxerre, blamed for being caught on the wrong side of Bernard Diomede as he smashed in the French side's first goal.

Van Gaal will toy with the idea of playing midfielder Ronald de Boer at the heart of the defence alongside Winston Bogarde or Mario Melchiot but, given the paucity of attacking options, de Boer would prefer to play further upfield.
In midfield, Jari Litmanen still has achilles tendon problems, Richard Witschge has had surgery on a toe infection, Peter Hoekstra has had a tendon operation and Kiki Musampa is carrying an injury.
Marc Overmars and striker Patrick Kluivert will play, but both look short of match fitness after lengthy lay-offs and have been hit by the loss of confidence that has infected the entire team.

While the Dutch champions suffer huge selection problems and continue to plunder the reserve team to field a full side, Feyenoord coach Arie Haan can draw on almost a full squad for Sunday's league clash.
Haan was doubly pleased after Tuesday's UEFA Cup third round first-leg trip to Tenerife -- a goalless draw which sets them up nicely for the return, and no injuries.

Of the regulars, Argentine defender Patricio Graff is into a four-match supension after head-butting NAC striker Yassine Abdellaoui last week, while midfielder Jean-Paul van Gastel is a long-term casualty after breaking a leg early in the season.
Defender George Boateng returns after suspension.
Haan is likely to stick to the side that earned the creditable draw in Spain, with Ed de Goey in goal and Boateng, Geoffrey Claeys, Henk Fraser and Bernard Schuiteman in defence.
The defence has conceeded only 18 goals in 16 matches, but this tally includes seven against PSV in a bizarre top-of-the-table encounter last month.
Libero Ronald Koeman will play in front of the back-four, linking up with winger Gaston Taument, Kees van Wonderen and Giovanni van Bronckhorst.
Haan will stick to his twin striker formation, with Swede Henryk Larsson, Feyenoord's leading marksman with five goals, alongside Argentine Pablo Sanchez. Feyenoord have scored 27 goals this season.
Feyenoord: Ed de Goey, George Boateng, Geoffrey Claeys, Henk Fraser, Ronald Koeman, Bernard Schuiteman; Kees van Wonderen, Giovanni van Bronckhorst, Pablo Sanchez, Gaston Taument, Henryk Larsson.
Ajax Amsterdam: Edwin van der Sar, Santos, Winston Bogarde, Mario Melchiot, Menno Willems, Ronald de Boer, Arnold Scholten, Nordin Wooter, Tijani Babangida, Marc Overmars, Patrick Kluivert.
